The thresholds (mixed>=24/96, exposed_streams>=8/12 with >=2 mixed pools each) were frozen in V3 before any E1-A outcome existed; the gate is evaluated only after all 96 K=8 pools are frozen; no task/pool may be replaced or dropped afterward; borderline values fail (23/96 fails, 7/12 fails, 1-mixed-pool stream does not count as exposed); and the family >=4/6 gate is explicitly separated and does not control pooled E1-B authority. The gate measures pre-treatment availability of mixed-pool contrast needed to identify delta_K, which is a design property, not an effectiveness statistic.",
  "outcome_selection_assessment": "No path in the orchestrator or adjudicator inspects mixed/support outcomes early to selectively stop, replace, rerun, or omit tasks. The orchestrator runs all 12 streams to completion before computing any support quantity; support is computed only after all 96 pools are frozen; the adjudicator independently recomputes from frozen pools. Technical failures stop execution with a stale lock preserved and are never treated as scientific failures or replaced based on scores. The reserve-integrity lane exists only for pre-execution file-integrity failure, not for model failure or bad outcomes, and is never invoked by the orchestrator.",
  "split_and_unit_assessment": "The bound split manifest contains exactly 12 e1_update_streams, each with 8 unique tasks, totaling 96 unique tasks (verified: no duplicates across streams). The e1_update_streams are disjoint from development (12 tasks), e0_calibration, e1_common_heldout_probe (18 tasks), e1_update_reserve_integrity_only, e3_future_streams, and e3_future_reserve_integrity_only. The orchestrator enforces 96 unique tasks and stream-order equality with the frozen contract. Suite and split manifest SHAs match the contract bindings.",
  "authorization_scope_assessment": "The new fail-closed execution_scope check in run_e2_r17_actor_pool.py, combined with the orchestrator's own scope validation, binds allowed_modes=['e1'], the exact 96 allowed_task_ids (orchestrator requires set equality with the frozen 96), exact_k=8, suite/split manifest SHAs, initial-skill SHA (required_skill_pre_sha256), resolved-model identity, identity-artifact SHA, max_turns, max_output_tokens, and provider-budget limits. The orchestrator additionally requires authority.e1_a=true and authority.e1_b=false. A non-initial skill is permitted only with a completed updater receipt bound to the same contract and authorization SHA; for E1-A the initial skill path is the default and any updater receipt is rejected. The proposed authorization cannot be trivially misused to run out-of-scope tasks, wrong K, or noninitial skills: out-of-scope task IDs are rejected by both the runner scope check and the orchestrator set-equality check; K drift is rejected by exact_k; noninitial skill without a bound receipt is rejected, and the E1-A orchestrator never supplies one.",
  "checkpoint_resume_assessment": "Both layers are sound. run_actor_rollout immediately persists the trajectory and content-addressed r17_trajectory_ref.json and reuses it only after revalidating the trajectory SHA and, when budgeted, the ledger/ref binding (unit id, unit claim count, total counter monotonicity). The orchestrator persists per-task prefix/K pools, per-stream summaries, appends+fsyncs completed_streams.jsonl, SHA-revalidates completed streams and rollouts before reuse (verify_stream_receipt checks summary SHA, pool files, trajectory SHAs, and budget ledger/ref consistency), and executes only missing streams. If interrupted inside an 8-rollout task, resuming after explicit stale-lock adjudication reuses completed rollouts via their refs and does not duplicate completed provider calls; the never-released budget claims deliberately over-count ambiguous in-flight calls so a resume cannot reset possible provider consumption.",
  "stale_lock_assessment": "The orchestrator intentionally leaves .exclusive.lock after any failed subprocess: acquire_lock uses O_CREAT|O_EXCL, the finally block closes the fd but only unlinks the lock when success=True, and a stream failure raises before success is set, preserving the lock for manual inspection. This is appropriately fail-closed for known MCP 502/timeout semantics. Successful completion removes the lock, which is correct; ordinary exception handling does not remove a lock that should remain because the unlink is gated strictly on the success flag.",
  "provider_budget_assessment": "The ceiling is now structurally enforced by a fail-closed pre-I/O accounting guard, not merely by the agent runtime. The ProviderBudgetLedger (SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE, synchronous=FULL, shared across stream subprocesses) requires a transactional claim before every provider generation call; claims are bound to the exact contract SHA, authorization SHA, global limit 7680, and per-unit limit 10; claims are never released after error/crash; the 11th per-unit call and the 7681st global call are rejected before provider I/O (tested, 21/21 PASS, zero provider I/O in tests). The ArkPlanReactLLM records claim ids in receipts, the trajectory ref records the claim bundle hash and counter state, and resume revalidates the ledger/ref binding. The prior P0 is repaired; no additional pre-call guard is needed.",

The identity artifact SHA is bound in the authorization scope and revalidated by both the orchestrator and the runner; retry=0 and thinking=disabled are set in the adapter and recorded in receipts. The qualification resolving deepseek-v4-pro to deepseek-v4-pro-ga-260813 with retry=0/thinking disabled is bound via identity_artifact_sha256.",
  "support_adjudicator_assessment": "adjudicate_e2_r17_e1_a_pool_support.py independently recomputes the 96 exact K=8 pools from disk, revalidates every trajectory SHA, recomputes the mixed total, per-stream mixed counts, exposed streams, and per-family support directly from the frozen pools (not trusting summary intermediates), and requires the no-updater condition (updater_calls==0) and e1_b_authority==False before returning PASS/STOP. It does not grant E1-B execution authority: authority.execute_e1_b is False and the PASS status only permits preparing a separate E1-B contract. The family gate is recorded but explicitly does not control primary E1-B authorization.",
  "updater_separation_assessment": "E1-A cannot call MindMemOS SkillEvolver or evaluate learned skills. The orchestrator and runner contain no updater invocation path for mode e1 with the initial skill; the non-initial-skill path requires an updater receipt that the E1-A orchestrator never supplies and the contract forbids; skill_mutation_allowed=false; updater_calls is asserted to be 0 in both the orchestrator summary and the adjudicator. E1-A output is only frozen pools plus support. Even a support PASS requires a separate immutable E1-B contract with fresh updater identity requalification and WIN-A/WIN-B negative-control-first logic, as encoded in the adjudicator next_gate and the V3 plan.",
  "remaining_blockers": [],
  "nonblocking_notes": [
    "The actor runner's validate_authority retains a readability path for historical authorization artifacts that lack execution_scope; this is intentional for replay and does not weaken E1-A because the E1-A orchestrator independently requires the scoped fields (allowed_modes==['e1'], exact 96-task set equality, exact_k=8) before launching any subprocess.",
    "The per-unit budget claim check on resume requires exact equality between the ledger unit count and the ref's provider_budget_unit_claimed_after; because claims are never released, a rollout that crashed mid-flight and is being re-run after quarantine will correctly fail reuse of any partial ref and quarantine the partial workdir, so no completed-call duplication occurs.",
    "The support adjudicator returns exit code 3 on support failure; operators and downstream tooling should treat this as an expected STOP signal, not a crash.",
    "The provider budget deliberately over-counts ambiguous calls (claims never released); the final summary asserts total_claimed >= total_provider_calls, so the declared 7680 ceiling is conservative and the actual receipt count may be lower."

  "e1_a_recommendation": "ALLOW_SEPARATE_FROZEN_E1_A_AUTHORIZATION",
  "e1_b_recommendation": "HOLD",
  "paper_claim_authority": false,
  "single_sentence_verdict": "The E1-A V2 draft contract and bound code implement a legitimate predeclared pre-treatment support gate over exactly 96 frozen tasks with fail-closed authorization scoping, checkpoint/resume, stale-lock, provider-budget, and model-identity enforcement, so I recommend minting a separate SHA-bound E1-A authorization for pool generation/support measurement only, with E1-B, held-out evaluation, and paper claims remaining unauthorized."

review.authorization_scope_assessment: The new fail-closed execution_scope check in run_e2_r17_actor_pool.py, combined with the orchestrator's own scope validation, binds allowed_modes=['e1'], the exact 96 allowed_task_ids (orchestrator requires set equality with the frozen 96), exact_k=8, suite/split manifest SHAs, initial-skill SHA (required_skill_pre_sha256), resolved-model identity, identity-artifact SHA, max_turns, max_output_tokens, and provider-budget limits. The orchestrator additionally requires authority.e1_a=true and authority.e1_b=false. A non-initial skill is permitted only with a completed updater receipt bound to the same contract and authorization SHA; for E1-A the initial skill path is the default and any updater receipt is rejected. The proposed authorization cannot be trivially misused to run out-of-scope tasks, wrong K, or noninitial skills: out-of-scope task IDs are rejected by both the runner scope check and the orchestrator set-equality check; K drift is rejected by exact_k; noninitial skill without a bound receipt is rejected, and the E1-A orchestrator never supplies one.
review.checkpoint_resume_assessment: Both layers are sound. run_actor_rollout immediately persists the trajectory and content-addressed r17_trajectory_ref.json and reuses it only after revalidating the trajectory SHA and, when budgeted, the ledger/ref binding (unit id, unit claim count, total counter monotonicity). The orchestrator persists per-task prefix/K pools, per-stream summaries, appends+fsyncs completed_streams.jsonl, SHA-revalidates completed streams and rollouts before reuse (verify_stream_receipt checks summary SHA, pool files, trajectory SHAs, and budget ledger/ref consistency), and executes only missing streams. If interrupted inside an 8-rollout task, resuming after explicit stale-lock adjudication reuses completed rollouts via their refs and does not duplicate completed provider calls; the never-released budget claims deliberately over-count ambiguous in-flight calls so a resume cannot reset possible provider consumption.
review.model_identity_assessment: The bound actor runner enforces the resolved identity on every provider receipt and fails on drift. ArkPlanReactLLM._respond compares the resolved model on every response (including the get-poll recovery path) against required_resolved_model and raises on mismatch; run_actor_rollout additionally asserts that the set of resolved models across all receipts equals exactly {deepseek-v4-pro-ga-260813}. The identity artifact SHA is bound in the authorization scope and revalidated by both the orchestrator and the runner; retry=0 and thinking=disabled are set in the adapter and recorded in receipts. The qualification resolving deepseek-v4-pro to deepseek-v4-pro-ga-260813 with retry=0/thinking disabled is bound via identity_artifact_sha256.
nonblocking_notes: The actor runner's validate_authority retains a readability path for historical authorization artifacts that lack execution_scope; this is intentional for replay and does not weaken E1-A because the E1-A orchestrator independently requires the scoped fields (allowed_modes==['e1'], exact 96-task set equality, exact_k=8) before launching any subprocess.

The per-unit budget claim check on resume requires exact equality between the ledger unit count and the ref's provider_budget_unit_claimed_after; because claims are never released, a rollout that crashed mid-flight and is being re-run after quarantine will correctly fail reuse of any partial ref and quarantine the partial workdir, so no completed-call duplication occurs.
The support adjudicator returns exit code 3 on support failure; operators and downstream tooling should treat this as an expected STOP signal, not a crash.

The provider budget deliberately over-counts ambiguous calls (claims never released); the final summary asserts total_claimed >= total_provider_calls, so the declared 7680 ceiling is conservative and the actual receipt count may be lower.
review.outcome_selection_assessment: No path in the orchestrator or adjudicator inspects mixed/support outcomes early to selectively stop, replace, rerun, or omit tasks. The orchestrator runs all 12 streams to completion before computing any support quantity; support is computed only after all 96 pools are frozen; the adjudicator independently recomputes from frozen pools. Technical failures stop execution with a stale lock preserved and are never treated as scientific failures or replaced based on scores. The reserve-integrity lane exists only for pre-execution file-integrity failure, not for model failure or bad outcomes, and is never invoked by the orchestrator.
review.provider_budget_assessment: The ceiling is now structurally enforced by a fail-closed pre-I/O accounting guard, not merely by the agent runtime. The ProviderBudgetLedger (SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE, synchronous=FULL, shared across stream subprocesses) requires a transactional claim before every provider generation call; claims are bound to the exact contract SHA, authorization SHA, global limit 7680, and per-unit limit 10; claims are never released after error/crash; the 11th per-unit call and the 7681st global call are rejected before provider I/O (tested, 21/21 PASS, zero provider I/O in tests). The ArkPlanReactLLM records claim ids in receipts, the trajectory ref records the claim bundle hash and counter state, and resume revalidates the ledger/ref binding. The prior P0 is repaired; no additional pre-call guard is needed.
review.single_sentence_verdict: The E1-A V2 draft contract and bound code implement a legitimate predeclared pre-treatment support gate over exactly 96 frozen tasks with fail-closed authorization scoping, checkpoint/resume, stale-lock, provider-budget, and model-identity enforcement, so I recommend minting a separate SHA-bound E1-A authorization for pool generation/support measurement only, with E1-B, held-out evaluation, and paper claims remaining unauthorized.
review.split_and_unit_assessment: The bound split manifest contains exactly 12 e1_update_streams, each with 8 unique tasks, totaling 96 unique tasks (verified: no duplicates across streams). The e1_update_streams are disjoint from development (12 tasks), e0_calibration, e1_common_heldout_probe (18 tasks), e1_update_reserve_integrity_only, e3_future_streams, and e3_future_reserve_integrity_only. The orchestrator enforces 96 unique tasks and stream-order equality with the frozen contract. Suite and split manifest SHAs match the contract bindings.
review.stale_lock_assessment: The orchestrator intentionally leaves .exclusive.lock after any failed subprocess: acquire_lock uses O_CREAT|O_EXCL, the finally block closes the fd but only unlinks the lock when success=True, and a stream failure raises before success is set, preserving the lock for manual inspection. This is appropriately fail-closed for known MCP 502/timeout semantics. Successful completion removes the lock, which is correct; ordinary exception handling does not remove a lock that should remain because the unlink is gated strictly on the success flag.
review.support_adjudicator_assessment: adjudicate_e2_r17_e1_a_pool_support.py independently recomputes the 96 exact K=8 pools from disk, revalidates every trajectory SHA, recomputes the mixed total, per-stream mixed counts, exposed streams, and per-family support directly from the frozen pools (not trusting summary intermediates), and requires the no-updater condition (updater_calls==0) and e1_b_authority==False before returning PASS/STOP. It does not grant E1-B execution authority: authority.execute_e1_b is False and the PASS status only permits preparing a separate E1-B contract. The family gate is recorded but explicitly does not control primary E1-B authorization.
review.support_gate_assessment: The gate is a legitimate predeclared identifiability/support gate, not method-outcome selection. The thresholds (mixed>=24/96, exposed_streams>=8/12 with >=2 mixed pools each) were frozen in V3 before any E1-A outcome existed; the gate is evaluated only after all 96 K=8 pools are frozen; no task/pool may be replaced or dropped afterward; borderline values fail (23/96 fails, 7/12 fails, 1-mixed-pool stream does not count as exposed); and the family >=4/6 gate is explicitly separated and does not control pooled E1-B authority. The gate measures pre-treatment availability of mixed-pool contrast needed to identify delta_K, which is a design property, not an effectiveness statistic.
review.updater_separation_assessment: E1-A cannot call MindMemOS SkillEvolver or evaluate learned skills. The orchestrator and runner contain no updater invocation path for mode e1 with the initial skill; the non-initial-skill path requires an updater receipt that the E1-A orchestrator never supplies and the contract forbids; skill_mutation_allowed=false; updater_calls is asserted to be 0 in both the orchestrator summary and the adjudicator. E1-A output is only frozen pools plus support. Even a support PASS requires a separate immutable E1-B contract with fresh updater identity requalification and WIN-A/WIN-B negative-control-first logic, as encoded in the adjudicator next_gate and the V3 plan.
